vt_4k_chain_4_first_pass.interpretation: First pass after 5 fails. Could be (a) stochastic instance draw — vt@4K chain=4 is 1 test item per run, and the generator may produce variable-difficulty problems, (b) fix in the RULER generator from the new unit tests (a2f5b2b), (c) a side-effect of other changes (DuoAttention calibration aabc2bf). Cannot determine from N=1 pass.

frequent_word_jump.r41: 100% on all three fw tasks (4K w=4, 16K w=5, 16K w=7)
frequent_word_jump.interpretation: Three tasks jumping uniformly from 33% to 100% is too coordinated for random draw — strongly suggests a bug fix or scoring change in the fw generator/gate. Most likely from commit a2f5b2b (31 new unit tests for RULER generators) which probably caught and fixed a bug. NOTE: the TOTAL of 3 per task in prior runs is 1/3, which with 3 items per task maps to 'always got 1 of 3' — consistent with a single-correct-answer generator producing a deterministic 1/3 score, not random. Fixed in R41.

mmlu_pro_45pct.interpretation: First measurement against MMLU-Pro for this model. 45% overall puts Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B in the general-knowledge-capable range but nowhere near GPT-4 (70%+). Category profile is interesting — very strong on psychology (100%), weak on chemistry/law/philosophy. This is expected for a coding-tuned model: structured reasoning > domain-specific trivia.

profiler_task_8.cpu_pct_interpretation: Dramatically higher than prior runs (R32-40: medians 8-16%). MMLU-Pro Phase 3c is CPU-heavy — likely subprocess-based eval with text extraction and answer parsing. The prior runs' 'benchmark is GPU-bound, not CPU-bound' conclusion was WRONG for MMLU-Pro workloads. The benchmark is GPU-bound only for the model-forward-pass phases (NIAH, RULER, HumanEval). MMLU-Pro is substantially CPU-bound.
